title: Synthesis of an Intein-mediated Artificial Protein Hydrogel
protocol: PCR amplify CutA and NpuN genes from plasmids pET30-CutA-Tip110 and KanR-IntRBS-NpuNC-CFN11, respectively.
Digest these fragments with the appropriate restriction enzymes.
Insert these fragments sequentially into the pET26b vector between the T7 promoter and a C-terminal 6xHistidine tag to generate N (Figure 2A).
PCR amplify NpuC, CutA, and S fragment [AG3(PEG)] from plasmid KanR-IntRBS-NpuNC-CFN11, pET30-CutA-Tip110, and pQE9 AC10Atrp, respectively.
Digest these fragments with the appropriate restriction enzymes.
Insert these fragments sequentially into the pET26b vector between T7 promoter and a C-terminal 6xHistidine to generate C (Figure 2B).
PCR amplify CutA using primers containing a SH3lig (PPPALPPKRRR) and a flexible linker (GGGGS)2 to generate fragment SH3lig-CutA.
Replace the CutA gene from C with fragment SH3lig-CutA.
Amplify the SH3 gene from plasmid pJD757 using the appropriate primers.
Fuse the GFP gene into the pET26b vector between the T7 promoter and a C-terminal 6xHistidine tag.
Transform 50 μl of chemically competent Escherichia coli BL21(DE3) with the appropriate expression plasmid.
Serially dilute transformed cells and plate them on LB/agar plates containing 50 μg/ml kanamycin.
Incubate plates at 37 °C for ~15 hr.
Resuspend all colonies from a plate containing 50-100 colonies in 5 ml of LB broth.
Transfer suspension to 1 L LB broth containing kanamycin (50 μg/ml) and grow cells at 37 °C with shaking at 250 rpm.
Monitor the absorbance at 600 nm (OD600).
Grow culture until OD600 ~0.8.
For C and C-SH3lig, add IPTG to the culture (1 mM final concentration) and incubate at 37 °C for 4 hr while shaking at 250 rpm.
For N and SH3-GFP, cool the culture to ~18 °C by immersing the culture flask in an ice water bath for ~5 min.
Add IPTG to the culture (1 mM final concentration) and incubate at 18 °C for 14-18 hr while shaking at 250 rpm.
Centrifuge the culture at 6,000 x g for 20 min at 4 °C to collect the pellet.
Store cell pellet at -80 °C until use.
Resuspend cell pellets in Buffer A at 10 ml/g of wet pellet.
Immerse the suspension in an ice-water bath.
Disrupt cells by sonication with settings: Amp 10, pulse for 1 second and pause for 6 seconds, repeating for 1 minute.
Centrifuge the lysate at 16,000 x g for 20 minutes at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in Buffer DA containing 8 M urea.
Centrifuge the suspension at 16,000 x g for 20 minutes at 4 °C.
Pass the supernatant through a 5 ml Ni-nitrilotriacetic acid (NTA) column previously equilibrated with buffer DA.
Wash the column with 30 ml of Buffer DA supplemented with 45 mM imidazole.
Elute purified protein using 20 ml of Buffer DA supplemented with 150 mM imidazole.

Reduce urea concentration in the protein sample to less than 1 mM by dialysis in DPBS buffer at 4 °C overnight or through repeated cycles of centrifugation and dilution using a 30 kDa ultra-filtration spin column.
Add dithiothreitol (DTT) to the purified protein to achieve a final concentration of 2 mM.
Concentrate the protein to approximately 100 mg/ml by centrifugation through a 30 kDa ultra-filtration spin column at 2,800 x g and 4 °C.
Aliquot the concentrated protein and store at -80 °C until use.
Resuspend cell pellets in Buffer B (pH 6.0) supplemented with 1x protease inhibitor cocktail at a ratio of 10 ml/g wet pellet.
Disrupt cell suspension by sonication.
Centrifuge the lysate at 16,000 x g for 20 minutes at 4 °C.
Keep the supernatant from the centrifugation step.
Pass the soluble lysate through a 5-ml Ni-NTA column previously equilibrated with buffer B.
Wash the column with Buffer B supplemented with 45 mM imidazole.
Elute the target protein in 20 ml of Buffer B supplemented with 150 mM imidazole.
Reduce NaCl concentration to <1 mM following a specified procedure for C-SH3lig samples.
Load the target protein onto a 5-ml anion exchanger beaded agarose matrix column previously equilibrated with sodium phosphate buffer (50 mM, pH 7.0).
Elute target protein from the ion-exchange column by running a gradient from a solution containing 10 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0 to a solution supplemented with 1 M NaCl.
Take samples during protein elution and pool samples with the highest purity based on SDS-PAGE analysis.
Buffer exchange the purified protein into DPBS buffer as described in protocol section 3.1.7.
Add DTT to the purified protein to achieve a final concentration of 2 mM.
Concentrate the protein to approximately 100 mg/ml using a 30 kDa ultra-filtration spin column.
Aliquot and store concentrated protein at -80 °C until use.
Resuspend cell pellets using Buffer A at a ratio of 10 ml/g of wet pellet.
Disrupt the resuspended pellet by sonication as described in 3.1.2.
Centrifuge the lysate at 16,000 x g for 20 minutes at 4 °C and collect the supernatant.
Pass the supernatant through a 5-ml Ni-NTA column previously equilibrated with Buffer A.
Wash the column with 30 ml of Buffer A supplemented with 45 mM imidazole.
Elute purified protein using 20 ml of Buffer A supplemented with 150 mM imidazole.
Buffer exchange the purified protein into DPBS buffer using an approach similar to that described in 3.1.7.
Concentrate the protein to approximately 150 mg/ml using a 30 kDa ultra-filtration spin column as described in 3.1.8.
Aliquot and store the purified protein at -80 °C until use.
Dilute each purified protein in double-distilled water to reduce the concentration of NaCl to approximately 1 mM.
Mix samples with 2x SDS sample buffer (0.5 M Tris-HCl, pH 6.8, 20% Glycerol, 10% w/v SDS, 0.1 % w/v bromo-phenol blue, 2% β-mercaptoethanol).
Incubate the samples at 95 °C for 5 minutes.
Load samples onto a 12% SDS-PAGE gel.
Carry out electrophoresis at a constant voltage of 200 V for approximately 50 minutes.
Stain protein in the gels with Coomassie brilliant blue R250 following standard protocols.
Calculate the volume needed for each concentrated protein to achieve a final concentration of 1.6 mM in a 100 μl sample hydrogel.
Mix C (x μl, as calculated) with 5% NaN3 (10 μl).
Add 100 mM DTT (5 μl) to the mixture.
Mix N (y μl, as calculated) into the solution.
Add DPBS buffer ((85 - x - y) μl) to achieve a final volume of 100 μl.
Manually mix all components via a swirling motion using a pipette tip.
Centrifuge the mixture for 2 min at 8,000 x g to remove air bubbles.
Incubate the mixture at room temperature overnight to allow intein trans-splicing reaction completion.
Confirm hydrogel formation by turning tube upside down.
Estimate intein trans-splicing yield by checking samples on a SDS-PAGE gel before step 4.2 and after step 4.5.
Combine C-SH3lig and SH3-GFP at a 1:1 molar ratio in a microcentrifuge tube to make a GFP-functionalized hydrogel.
Incubate the mixture at room temperature for 30 min.
Add 5% NaN3, 100 mM DTT, and DPBS to the tube.
Mix the sample by swirling motion with a pipette tip.
Centrifuge the mixture at 8,000 x g for 2 min.
Incubate the mixture overnight in the dark to form hydrogel encapsulating SH3-GFP.
Prepare a stock solution of HRP in DPBS.
Combine C (x μl) with HRP (2 μl), 5% NaN3 (3 μl) and DTT (1.5 μl of 100 mM).
Add N (y μl) and DPBS (23.5 - x - y μl) to the mixture.
Mix the components thoroughly using a pipette tip with a swirling motion.
Centrifuge the mixture at 8,000 x g for 2 min.
Incubate the mixture at room temperature overnight.
Submerge the hydrogel in 1 ml of reaction cocktail containing N,N-dimethyl-p-phenylene diamine (5.8 mM), phenol (5.8 mM) and tert-butyl hydroperoxide (2.9 mM) in n-heptane.
Manually disrupt the gel using a pipette tip to increase contact surface area with the solvent.
Detect HRP product by measuring optical absorbance of samples at 546 nm in a plate reader.
